title: Bangladesh | Bank Governance, Compliance, Code of Conduct and Harassment Prevention
tagline: Apply the Bank Company Act, BRPD board rules, Bangladesh Bank's 2026 internal control guidelines, its Code of Conduct and the 2026 Labour Act harassment duties.
description:
This quest teaches the governance, compliance and conduct rules that apply to conventional scheduled banks in Bangladesh. It is based on the **Bank Company Act 1991** (as amended in 2023), **BRPD Circular 02 of 2024** on boards and directors with its 2025 follow-ups, Bangladesh Bank's **Guidelines on Internal Control Management System** (BRPD-2 Circular 03, July 2026), the **Guidelines on Foundation Training** (BRPD-1 Circular 10, May 2026), Bangladesh Bank's **Code of Conduct for Banks and NBFIs**, the **Public Interest Information Disclosure Act 2011** and the **Bangladesh Labour (Amendment) Act 2026** (new sections 332 and 332A).

Section 5.4.3 of the 2026 internal control guidelines requires every bank's compliance function, with HR, to deliver a **mandatory, role-based compliance training programme** built on its compliance risk assessment, and banks must restructure to the new system by 31 December 2026. The Code requires staff training on integrity, and the amended Labour Act requires employers to train workers on violence and harassment. This quest supports those duties for staff, managers, ICMS, HR and compliance teams, company secretaries and directors.

In five stages you join the Compliance Division of a fictional Bangladeshi bank, from the boardroom to the branch.

The quest builds knowledge and does not replace your bank's own policies, code of conduct and procedures; always follow them and the latest Bangladesh Bank instructions.
audience: All officers and staff of scheduled banks in Bangladesh who must complete role-based compliance and code of conduct training
Compliance, internal control and internal audit staff working under the 2026 ICMS guidelines
HR and training staff who design foundation, compliance and harassment-prevention training
Branch managers and supervisors who handle conduct issues, whistleblower concerns and harassment complaints
Company secretaries, directors and senior managers who apply the board and committee rules
outcomes: Explain how the Bank Company Act, section 45 directions, BRPD circulars and bank policies fit together
Apply the rules on board composition, fit and proper directors, Bangladesh Bank approvals and board committees
Describe the three lines of defence, the heads of audit and compliance, and the compliance risk management cycle
Design mandatory, role-based compliance training that meets section 5.4.3 of the 2026 ICMS guidelines
Apply the Code of Conduct to gifts, conflicts and confidentiality, and use the whistleblower framework safely
Meet the Labour Act 2026 duties on harassment training and the section 332A complaints committee

sessions.title: The Legal Map: the Bank Company Act, Section 45 Directions and the Board
sessions.summary: See how the Bank Company Act 1991 (as amended in 2023), Bangladesh Bank's binding directions under section 45 and the BRPD circulars fit together, how a bank board must be built, and the powers Bangladesh Bank holds over directors and boards.
objectives: Place the Bank Company Act, section 45 directions, BRPD circulars, guidelines and the bank's own policies in order
Apply the rules on board size, independent directors, family limits, tenure and retirement
Explain when Bangladesh Bank's prior approval is needed for directors and alternate directors
Describe Bangladesh Bank's powers to remove directors and dissolve a board

cards.title: First day in the governance unit
cards.setting: Compliance Division, Krishnachura Bank PLC head office, Motijheel, Dhaka. 9:30 am.

lines.text: Welcome to Policies and Governance. I'm Mitali Sarkar, Head of Compliance. From today you help me keep the board, the bank and every desk inside the rules.
Tanvir Ahmed Chowdhury, company secretary. Fair warning: the board meets next week and a sponsor family has just nominated a new director.
Then the first question is not who the nominee is. It is which rules decide whether that person can sit on our board at all.
The Bank Company Act, the BRPD circular on boards, the later circular letters... people mix them up all the time.
That's our first stage: the Motijheel Charter. Learn the map and every later stage gets easier.
Your mission: build Krishnachura's governance, compliance, ethics and harassment-prevention programme before Bangladesh Bank's 31 December 2026 deadline for the new internal control system.

scenes.heading: The Act
scenes.narration: The Bank Company Act 1991, amended most recently in 2023, sets the core rules on directors, board committees, internal audit and Bangladesh Bank's powers.

scenes.heading: Section 45 directions
scenes.narration: Section 45 lets Bangladesh Bank give binding directions to all banks or to one bank, for example in the public interest or to protect depositors. Banks must obey them.

scenes.heading: Circulars and guidelines
scenes.narration: Most governance rules arrive this way: BRPD Circular 02 of 2024 on boards, the July 2026 internal control guidelines and the 2026 foundation training guidelines were all issued under section 45.

scenes.heading: Other laws
scenes.narration: Banks are also employers and companies. The Labour Act's harassment duties and the whistleblower protection law apply alongside banking law.

scenes.heading: The bank's own policies
scenes.narration: Finally, the board approves the bank's own code of conduct, compliance policy and training policy. They may go further than the regulator, never below it.

cards.title: Which rule wins?

items.label: Bank Company Act 1991
items.detail: Parliament's law; sections 15, 15B, 15C, 45, 46 and 47 shape boards and control.

items.label: Section 45 directions
items.detail: Binding circulars and circular letters, e.g. BRPD Circular 02/2024.

items.label: Bangladesh Bank guidelines
items.detail: Issued by circular: ICMS 2026, Code of Conduct 2017, foundation training 2026.

items.label: Other national laws
items.detail: Labour Act as amended in 2026; Public Interest Information Disclosure Act 2011.

items.label: Board-approved bank policies
items.detail: Must meet every layer above; may set higher standards.

cards.caption: Top = highest legal force. A bank policy that conflicts with a direction or the Act gives way.

cards.question: Krishnachura's head of HR asks why the bank must follow BRPD Circular 02 of 2024 when it is 'only a circular'. What is the best answer?
options: It was issued under sections 15 and 45 of the Bank Company Act, so it is a binding direction the bank must obey
It is guidance only; the bank may follow its own articles of association instead
It binds only state-owned banks, because they are directly supervised
It becomes binding only after the shareholders adopt it at the next AGM
cards.explanation: Paragraph 15 of the circular says it was issued under sections 15 and 45 of the Act. Section 45 makes such directions binding on the banks they address, private or state-owned.

cards.title: How a bank board is built
cards.body:
The Act (section 15(9)-(10)) and BRPD Circular 02/2024 (paragraph 3) set the shape of every board:

- **Members:** shareholder directors, representative directors of shareholder companies and **independent directors**; an approved alternate director may also sit.
- **Size:** at most **20** directors.
- **Independent directors:** at least **3** when the board has 20 members, at least **2** when it has fewer. An independent director is free of management and shareholders and has no past, present or future interest in the bank.
- **Families:** no more than **3** members of one family at a time, plus at most **2** representative directors for companies that family controls.
- **Representatives:** one company may send only **one** representative director; an individual shareholder cannot be represented by someone else.
- **Tenure:** no more than **12 consecutive years** (section 15AA), then a **3-year** break.
- **Rotation:** all directors retire at the first AGM; after that one-third retire each year by seniority and may stand again.

cards.title: Match the board rule to its number
cards.prompt: Each figure comes from section 15 of the Act or BRPD Circular 02/2024.

pairs.left: Independent directors on a smaller board
Family members serving at the same time
Consecutive years a director may serve
Directors retiring at each later AGM

cards.title: Krishnachura's board check

items.label: Directors
items.detail: Within the cap of 20 set by section 15(9).

items.label: Independent directors
items.detail: A board under 20 needs at least 2; Krishnachura has 3.

items.label: Members of the Rahman family
items.detail: The family limit is 3; a fourth nominee would breach it.

items.label: Longest-serving director
items.detail: Must step down at 12 consecutive years.

cards.caption: A fictional snapshot the company secretary prepares before every nomination.

cards.title: The fourth family member
cards.setting: Company secretary's office, two days before the board meeting.

lines.text: The nominee is Farzana Rahman, daughter of our chairman. Strong CV, fifteen years in business.
How many Rahmans sit on the board today?
Three. And her nomination letter comes from Rahman Textiles, which already has a representative director.
Then we have two problems before we even look at her experience: the family limit and the one-representative-per-company rule.
The chairman wants it on next week's agenda anyway. He says Bangladesh Bank can sort it out.

cards.title: The nomination on the agenda
cards.situation: Krishnachura's chairman asks the company secretary to place his daughter's nomination as a representative director of Rahman Textiles on the next board agenda. Three members of the Rahman family already sit on the 17-member board, and Rahman Textiles already has one representative director. The chairman says Bangladesh Bank will reject it if there is a problem, so the bank need not worry.

choices.text: Advise the chairman in writing that the nomination would breach the three-family-member limit and the one-representative-per-company rule, and keep it off the agenda unless the facts change.
choices.outcome: Best. The bank, not Bangladesh Bank, is first responsible for meeting section 15(10) and paragraph 3 of BRPD Circular 02. Clear written advice protects the board and the company secretary.

choices.text: Place it on the agenda but attach a compliance note listing the two breaches so directors can decide.
choices.outcome: Partly right. Flagging the breaches is good, but asking the board to approve a nomination the law forbids invites a decision that cannot stand and wastes Bangladesh Bank's time.

choices.text: Send it straight to Bangladesh Bank for prior approval and let the regulator decide.
choices.outcome: Poor. Prior approval is the last check, not a substitute for the bank's own compliance. The application itself would show the bank ignoring the Act.

choices.text: Approve it subject to another Rahman director resigning within six months.
choices.outcome: Poor. The limit applies at all times. A future resignation does not make an appointment lawful today.

items.label: Bank Company Act
items.detail: Parliament's core banking law.

items.label: 12-year limit runs
items.detail: Consecutive-term count starts from 28 January 2018 (BRPD 02/2024 para 3(j)).

items.label: Amendment Act
items.detail: Board, independent director and fitness rules reshaped; in force 26 June 2023.

items.label: BRPD Circular 02
items.detail: Board formation and directors' duties; replaced the 2013 circular.

items.label: Alternate directors
items.detail: BRPD Circular 01: Bangladesh Bank prior approval before they act.

items.label: Minutes must show dissent
items.detail: BRPD Circular Letter 14 on board and committee minutes.

items.label: Foundation training
items.detail: BRPD-1 Circular 10: 14-week course for new officers.

items.label: ICMS guidelines
items.detail: BRPD-2 Circular 03; banks restructure by 31 December 2026.

cards.back: Except in specialised banks, directors and the MD/CEO need Bangladesh Bank's approval before appointment, and cannot be removed or dismissed without its prior approval.
Bangladesh Bank may issue binding directions in the public interest, to protect depositors or to ensure proper management, and may remove or appoint a director under this power.
Bangladesh Bank may remove a chairman, director or chief executive, after giving a chance to show cause, to stop harm to depositors, misuse of funds, money laundering or TF.
If a board acts against the bank's or depositors' interests, Bangladesh Bank may dissolve it by written order for a set period, at most two years including extensions.
Since BRPD Circular 01 of 2025, an alternate director may not act or attend any board or committee meeting until Bangladesh Bank has approved the appointment.
A director who fails to repay a loan within two months of a notice through Bangladesh Bank loses the seat and cannot rejoin any bank board for a year after repaying.

cards.question: A director of Krishnachura will be abroad for four months. The board appoints an alternate, who wants to attend next Tuesday's audit committee. What do the rules say?
options: He may not attend: alternates cannot sit on board committees, and he needs Bangladesh Bank's prior approval before acting at all
He may attend once the bank has informed Bangladesh Bank, since only notice is required
He may attend board and committee meetings for up to three months without any approval
He may attend if the absent director signs a written proxy for that meeting
cards.explanation: BRPD Circular 02 (paragraph 6(e)) bars alternates from board committees, and BRPD Circular 01 of 2025 requires Bangladesh Bank's prior approval before an alternate acts or attends any board or committee meeting.

cards.title: Real case: Bangladesh Bank dissolves 15 bank boards (2025)
cards.body:
In its Monetary Policy Statement for July-December 2025, Bangladesh Bank reported that it had looked for weaknesses in bank boards that had contributed to banks' financial deterioration. It said it had, so far, **dissolved the boards of directors of 15 banks and restructured them** to restore effective governance and sound management. It also described a circular of 8 May 2025 on **transactions with bank-related persons or institutions**, tightening limits on credit to current directors, MDs/CEOs, significant shareholders, their families, ultimate beneficial owners and linked entities.

**Why it matters at your desk:** the powers in sections 45-47 are not theory. When a board fails, the regulator can replace it. The best defence is a board that is properly built, keeps out of day-to-day operations and gets honest reports from compliance and audit.

cards.title: Reading a Bangladesh Bank circular
cards.body:
- Many BRPD circulars are issued **in Bangla only**; the English title on the website is a summary. Read the original or an approved translation.
- Check the **legal basis** paragraph (usually section 45) and the **effective date** (often 'immediately').
- Read the **repeal paragraph**: it tells you which older circulars are gone.
- Check later **circular letters** that amend it, such as BRPD Circular Letter 14 of 2025 on minutes.
- Record each change in the bank's **regulatory obligations register** (Stage 3).

cards.title: Stage 1 take-aways
items: Directions under section 45 of the Bank Company Act, including BRPD circulars and guidelines, bind every bank they address.
A board has at most 20 directors, with at least 3 independent directors (at least 2 if the board is smaller).
No more than 3 family members may serve at once; directors may serve 12 consecutive years, then must wait 3.
Directors, the MD/CEO and alternate directors need Bangladesh Bank's prior approval before they act.
Bangladesh Bank can remove directors (section 46) and dissolve boards (section 47); in 2025 it reported dissolving 15 boards.

cards.prompt: Think of a decision at your bank that depended on a Bangladesh Bank circular. Did the people involved know which layer of the rules it came from? How would you check it next time?

quiz.question: Under which section of the Bank Company Act 1991 does Bangladesh Bank usually issue binding directions such as BRPD circulars?
options: Section 17
Section 15AA
Section 45
Section 47
quiz.explanation: Section 45 empowers Bangladesh Bank to issue directions to all banks or a particular bank, and the banks must comply. Section 47 is about dissolving a board, not issuing directions.

quiz.question: A bank board has 16 directors. What is the minimum number of independent directors?
options: Three
One
Two
Four
quiz.explanation: Section 15(9) and paragraph 3(c) of BRPD Circular 02/2024 require at least 3 independent directors on a 20-member board and at least 2 where the board has fewer than 20.

quiz.question: Which of these is the correct maximum size of a bank board under the Bank Company Act as amended in 2023?
options: 20 directors
15 directors
13 directors
25 directors, including the chair
quiz.explanation: Section 15(9) caps the board at 20 directors, including the independent directors.

quiz.question: A sponsor family already has three members on a bank board. It nominates a fourth as a shareholder director. What is the position?
options: It is allowed if the fourth member is an independent director
It is allowed if the family holds more than 10% of the shares
It is allowed once Bangladesh Bank waives the family limit by a letter to the board chair
The nomination breaches the limit of three family members serving at the same time
quiz.explanation: Section 15(10) and paragraph 3(d) of BRPD Circular 02 allow no more than three members of one family as directors at the same time. Family members cannot be independent directors in any case.

quiz.question: A director has served 12 consecutive years on Krishnachura's board. When can he next be appointed to the same board?
options: After a break of one year
After a break of three years
Immediately, if shareholders re-elect him
Never again at the same bank
quiz.explanation: Section 15AA limits consecutive service to 12 years; the person becomes eligible again at the same bank only after three years have passed.

quiz.question: What happens to directors at a bank company's annual general meetings after the first AGM?
options: One-third retire each year by seniority and may stand for re-election
All directors retire at every AGM and must be reappointed by the shareholders each year
Only independent directors retire, every three years
Directors serve until 12 years without retiring
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 3(i) of BRPD Circular 02/2024 says all directors retire at the first AGM and one-third retire at each later AGM by seniority, following the Companies Act schedule; they may be re-elected.

quiz.question: Bangladesh Bank believes a board's actions are harming depositors. Which power lets it dissolve the board by written order?
options: Section 15C of the Bank Company Act
Paragraph 14 of BRPD Circular 02/2024
Section 47 of the Bank Company Act
Section 332 of the Labour Act
quiz.explanation: Section 47 allows Bangladesh Bank to dissolve a board, with reasons recorded in writing, for a set period of no more than two years including extensions. Section 15C deals with internal audit.

quiz.question: Since January 2025, when may an alternate director first attend a board meeting?
options: As soon as the bank has notified Bangladesh Bank
Only after Bangladesh Bank has given prior approval of the appointment
Once the absent director has been abroad for one month
After the company secretary records the appointment in the minutes of the board
quiz.explanation: BRPD Circular 01 of 2025 ended the practice of alternates attending on notice alone: they may not act or attend board or committee meetings without Bangladesh Bank's prior approval.

quiz.question: Which of these may Bangladesh Bank do under section 46 of the Bank Company Act?
options: Fine an individual director for a missed board meeting
Order a sponsor family to sell all of its shares in the bank within thirty days of a notice
Appoint the bank's external auditor directly
Remove a chairman, director or chief executive after giving a chance to show cause
quiz.explanation: Section 46 lets Bangladesh Bank remove a chairman, director or chief executive, with reasons recorded, to prevent harm to the bank or depositors, misuse of funds, money laundering or TF, after a reasonable chance to show cause.

quiz.question: Krishnachura's draft board policy says the board may approve directors 'in line with the bank's articles even if a BRPD circular differs'. What should compliance advise?
options: Keep it: the articles prevail because shareholders approved them
Keep it for private banks but not for state-owned banks
Keep it until Bangladesh Bank raises an objection to it in a comprehensive inspection report
Delete it: directions under section 45 bind the bank regardless of its articles
quiz.explanation: Section 45 makes Bangladesh Bank's directions binding, and section 15(9)-(10) applies whatever a bank's articles say. A policy cannot permit what a binding direction forbids.

sessions.title: Fit and Proper Directors, Board Duties, Committees and Minutes
sessions.summary: Apply the fitness tests for directors, the approval process with Bangladesh Bank, the duties of the board and chair under BRPD Circular 02/2024, the three permitted board committees, meeting rules and the 2025 requirement to minute dissent.
objectives: Apply the fit and proper criteria for directors in section 15(6) and BRPD Circular 02/2024
Describe the board's duties and the limits on directors' involvement in credit and HR decisions
Explain the make-up and duties of the executive, audit and risk management committees
Apply the meeting and minuting rules, including BRPD Circular Letter 14 of 2025

cards.title: The nominee's file
cards.setting: Company secretary's office, Krishnachura Bank PLC, Motijheel.

lines.text: New nominee, different family this time: Mr. Aminul Haque, 34, managing director of a garments group. Twelve years in business.
Good start. What does his CIB report say?
A term loan to one of his group companies is classified as defaulted at another bank.
Professor Rokeya Begum, independent director and chair of the audit committee. If that is right, he cannot even be nominated. A default by an interested company counts.
And he wants a seat on the audit committee and the executive committee.
Welcome to the Boardroom Gate. Let's see who gets through it, and what they may do once inside.

cards.title: Fit and proper in five questions

scenes.heading: Experienced enough?
scenes.narration: A director needs at least ten years of management, business or professional experience, and must be at least thirty. Work done before the age of eighteen does not count.

scenes.heading: Clean record?
scenes.narration: No criminal conviction, no involvement in fraud or financial crime, no adverse court remarks, and no punishment for breaking a financial regulator's rules.

scenes.heading: Paying debts?
scenes.narration: Not a loan defaulter, personally or through interested companies, not a tax defaulter, never declared bankrupt, and not listed as a wilful defaulter in the last five years.

scenes.heading: Free of conflicts?
scenes.narration: Not a director, adviser or paid office holder at another bank, finance company, insurer or their subsidiaries, and not this bank's auditor, lawyer or consultant.

scenes.heading: Approved?
scenes.narration: The bank applies to Bangladesh Bank within seven working days of the board meeting or AGM, with declarations and CIB reports. The appointment runs only from Bangladesh Bank's approval.

items.label: Nomination
items.detail: Board nominates or AGM elects a candidate.

items.label: Eligibility screen
items.detail: Section 15(6) and BRPD 02/2024 para 4: age, experience, record, debts, conflicts.

items.label: Application
items.detail: Within 7 working days, signed by the MD/CEO, with forms, declarations and CIB reports.

items.label: Bangladesh Bank review
items.detail: Prior approval under section 15(4).

items.label: Seat taken
items.detail: Effective from the date of Bangladesh Bank's approval.

cards.question: Mr. Haque's group company has a defaulted loan at another bank. What does that mean for his nomination?
options: He is not eligible: a default by an interested company disqualifies him
He is eligible if his personal accounts are clean
He is eligible, but only as an independent director
He is eligible if the other bank reschedules the loan after he joins
cards.explanation: Paragraph 4(7) of BRPD Circular 02/2024 and section 15(6) of the Act exclude anyone who is a defaulter in his own name or through an interested institution.

cards.title: What the board must do, and must not do
cards.body:
Under sections 15B-15C of the Act and paragraph 10 of BRPD Circular 02/2024 the board is accountable for policy, risk management, internal control and internal audit. In practice it:

- Sets **strategy every year**, tracks it **quarterly** and sets KPIs for the CEO and the two tiers below.
- Approves **credit, risk, HR and budget** policies and delegates loan approval to management.
- Keeps **internal audit independent** and reviews the audit committee's report **quarterly**.
- Gives **special importance to staff training** and IT/MIS in the annual work plan.
- Adopts an **integrity policy, code of conduct and code of ethics** for all staff and sets high ethical standards.

**Limits:** no director may influence officers on a loan approval; the chair and directors may not interfere in appointments, promotions, transfers or discipline (except for the CEO and the two tiers below, which belong to the board); the chair has **no individual executive power**.

cards.title: Board business or management business?
cards.prompt: Sort each item by who decides it under BRPD Circular 02/2024.

items.text: Approving the bank's credit policy and delegation of loan powers
Setting KPIs for the CEO and the two tiers below
Adopting the code of conduct and code of ethics for all staff
Promoting a branch's senior officer under the service rules
Approving a specific SME loan within delegated powers
Transferring a cash officer from Sylhet to Khulna
Approving the purchase of land for a new branch
Deciding the shortlist for a probationary officer recruitment

cards.title: The three permitted committees

items.label: Independent directors
items.left: Audit: at least 2, and it is chaired by one
items.right: Executive and risk: no minimum set

items.label: Chair's term
items.left: 3 years; an ID cannot chair audit two terms in a row

items.label: Who cannot join
items.left: No executive committee member on audit; no alternate on any
items.right: Executive: at most one member of a family

items.label: Meetings
items.left: Audit and risk: at least 4 a year
items.right: Executive: as needed; decisions ratified by the board

cards.caption: Section 15B and BRPD Circular 02/2024 para 11 allow only these three committees; the company secretary is secretary to each.

cards.title: The chair's phone call
cards.setting: Audit committee chair's room, after a board meeting.

lines.text: The chairman phoned the Agrabad branch manager yesterday about a loan for a supplier. He says he only 'asked about progress'.
Sharmin Akter, Agrabad branch manager. He asked twice. The file is still with credit risk and my team felt pressure.
Paragraph 10 is clear: no director may influence officers on a loan approval, and the chair has no executive power of his own.
I want this minuted at the next board meeting. He will object, so I may have to record a note of dissent.
Since last August the minutes must record the discussion and any dissent in detail. I cannot leave it out.

cards.title: Pressure on a loan file
cards.situation: Krishnachura's chairman has twice phoned the Agrabad branch manager about a supplier's loan that is still with credit risk. The branch manager has told compliance. At the next board meeting, the chairman says the matter is 'not for the minutes' and asks the company secretary to leave it out. The audit committee chair disagrees.

choices.text: The company secretary minutes the discussion, the audit committee chair's objection and any note of dissent in full, and compliance reports the contact to the audit committee.
choices.outcome: Best. BRPD Circular Letter 14 of 2025 requires minutes to record discussions, dissenting views and notes of dissent in detail. Paragraph 10 forbids directors influencing loan approvals, so it belongs with the audit committee.

choices.text: Leave it out of the minutes but keep a private file note in the company secretary's office.
choices.outcome: Poor. A private note does not meet the duty to record discussions and dissent in the minutes, and it hides the issue from Bangladesh Bank's review of minutes.

choices.text: Minute only the decision taken, with a line that 'members discussed a loan matter'.
choices.outcome: Partly right but weak. A one-line summary is exactly what the 2025 circular letter was issued to stop; dissent and observations must be recorded properly.

choices.text: Ask the branch manager to approve the loan quickly so the dispute ends.
choices.outcome: Poor. That rewards the interference and exposes the branch manager to a credit decision made under pressure.

cards.title: Running a compliant board meeting
cards.prompt: Put the steps in the order BRPD Circular 02/2024 and Circular Letter 14/2025 expect.
steps: Agenda items are fixed; nothing outside the agenda may be considered
Memos reach directors at least two days before the meeting
Only directors, the MD and the company secretary attend; officers join only to present their item
The board discusses and decides; any director may record a note of dissent
Minutes record the discussion, all observations, dissent in detail and any Bangladesh Bank observer's views
Executive committee decisions taken between meetings are ratified at the next board meeting

items.label: Set strategy, approve policy
items.detail: The board's job: plan yearly, monitor quarterly.

items.label: Oversee and ask questions
items.detail: Chair may call for information or order an inquiry through the board.

items.label: Direct a loan or posting
items.detail: Forbidden: influence on credit, HR or daily operations.

items.label: Act alone as 'executive chair'
items.detail: Forbidden: the chair has no individual executive power.

cards.question: Krishnachura wants a 'board IT committee' to oversee its core banking upgrade. What does BRPD Circular 02/2024 allow?
options: No: only the executive, audit and risk management committees may be formed
Yes, if at least two independent directors sit on it
Yes, as a temporary sub-committee for up to one year
Yes, if Bangladesh Bank is told within seven days
cards.explanation: Paragraph 11 says the board forms an executive committee, an audit committee and a risk management committee, and no other permanent or temporary committee or sub-committee.

cards.title: Inside a fitness file at Krishnachura
cards.body:
Before the board even nominates a candidate, Tanvir's team builds a file:

- **CV and age proof:** at least 30 years old and 10 years' experience counted from age 18.
- **CIB reports** on the person and every interested company (for a representative director, also the shareholder company).
- **Declarations:** the candidate's declaration, a confidentiality declaration and, for independent directors, an extra declaration that he holds no shares and no interest in the bank.
- **Bank's certificate:** no default; whether family members sit on the board; no post at another bank, finance company or insurer; not the bank's auditor, lawyer or consultant; any past link with management.
- **Certified minutes** of the board meeting or AGM, signed off by the company secretary and the MD.

The MD signs the application and it goes to Bangladesh Bank within **seven working days**. After approval, the bank updates its director list, its website (with photos) and Bangladesh Bank's portal.

cards.title: Director training: what the circular says
cards.body: Paragraph 14 of BRPD Circular 02/2024 says in-country training **may be arranged** for directors on banking law, related laws and changed regulations. The wording is permissive, so treat it as good practice, not a set course. The audit, executive and risk committees, though, must have members who **understand the Bank Company Act, banking law, risks and their own duties**, so a short induction for every new director is the simplest way to show that.

cards.title: Stage 2 take-aways
items: Directors need 10 years' experience, a minimum age of 30, a clean record, no defaults and no conflicting posts.
Appointments take effect only on Bangladesh Bank's approval; the bank applies within seven working days.
The board sets policy and strategy, keeps audit independent, prioritises training and adopts the code of conduct.
Directors may not influence loans, postings or discipline; the chair has no individual executive power.
Only three committees are allowed, and minutes must record discussion and dissent in detail.

cards.prompt: If a director contacted you directly about a customer's file, what would you say, and who would you tell? Write the two sentences you would use.

quiz.question: What is the minimum age for a director of a bank company under BRPD Circular 02/2024?
options: 25 years
35 years
40 years
30 years
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 4(2) of BRPD Circular 02/2024 sets a minimum age of 30.

quiz.question: A candidate has 11 years of business experience, but three of those years were before she turned 18. Does she meet the experience test?
options: Yes: all 11 years count, because the 10-year minimum includes any work experience at all
No: work before age 18 does not count, leaving 8 years against a 10-year minimum
Yes, if the board certifies her as fit
No: the minimum is 15 years for any new director
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 4(1) requires at least 10 years of management, business or professional experience and says experience before age 18 is not considered.

quiz.question: Within what time must a bank apply to Bangladesh Bank for approval after a board meeting or AGM nominates or elects a director?
options: Within 7 working days
Within 30 days
Within 2 months
Before the next AGM
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 5 of BRPD Circular 02/2024 requires the application, signed by the MD/CEO, within seven working days of the board meeting or AGM.

quiz.question: A former deputy managing director of Krishnachura retired two years ago and is now nominated to its board. What applies?
options: He is eligible at once because he knows the bank well
He is eligible only as an independent director
He is not eligible until five years after his service with the bank ended
He is eligible at once if he gives up his pension and any other benefits from the bank
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 4(12) of BRPD Circular 02/2024 bars a person who worked in the same bank until five years have passed since that employment ended.

quiz.question: Which committee may an executive committee member NOT join?
options: The risk management committee
The audit committee
Any committee chaired by the board chair
The executive committee of a subsidiary
quiz.explanation: Section 15B(2) of the Act and paragraph 11.2 of BRPD Circular 02/2024 require the audit committee to be formed of directors who are not executive committee members.

quiz.question: What is the maximum size of a bank's audit committee and its minimum number of independent directors?
options: Seven members, at least one independent director
Five members, all of them independent directors
Three members, at least two independent directors
Five members, at least two of them independent directors
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 11.2(a) of BRPD Circular 02/2024 sets a maximum of five members including at least two independent directors, with the chair chosen from the independent directors.

quiz.question: Who may attend a bank's board meeting besides the directors?
options: Any senior executive whom the chair invites, for the whole meeting, if minuted
Shareholders holding more than 5% of the shares
The bank's legal adviser and external auditor as observers
Only the MD and company secretary; officers only while presenting an item
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 12.1 of BRPD Circular 02/2024 limits attendance to directors, the MD and the company secretary; an officer may attend, not full-time, only to present a related matter, and outsiders may never attend.

quiz.question: What did BRPD Circular Letter 14 of 4 August 2025 require?
options: Board meetings must be held at least twice a month
Minutes must record discussions, dissent and Bangladesh Bank observers' views
Every director must attend at least one training course on banking law every year
Alternate directors may attend audit committees with notice
quiz.explanation: The circular letter found minutes often omitted discussions and dissent, and directed banks to record discussions, all observations, notes of dissent in detail and the views of any Bangladesh Bank observer.

quiz.question: The board chair wants to visit two branches to see how a new lending product works. Is that allowed?
options: No, a chair may never visit a branch
Yes, and he may approve pending loans while there
Yes, as part of the board's oversight role, but he may not direct daily operations
Only if Bangladesh Bank gives its prior approval for each visit in writing, seven days ahead
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 10.2 of BRPD Circular 02/2024 lets the chair visit branches or financing activities as part of oversight, while forbidding involvement or interference in daily administration.

quiz.question: Paragraph 10 of BRPD Circular 02/2024 asks the board to give special importance to which item in its annual work plan?
options: Training to build staff skills, along with modern IT and MIS
Branch expansion targets for each district
Annual salary increases for all staff
Sponsorship of sports and cultural events
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 10.1(d) says the board shall give special importance to training for officers' skill development and to modern technology and MIS, and include them in the annual work plan.

sessions.title: The 2026 Internal Control Guidelines: Three Lines, Compliance Risk and Role-Based Training
sessions.summary: Work through Bangladesh Bank's July 2026 Guidelines on Internal Control Management System: the three lines of defence, the heads of internal audit and compliance, the compliance risk management framework, observation tracking and the mandatory role-based compliance training in section 5.4.3.
objectives: Explain the three lines of defence as the 2026 ICMS guidelines define them
Describe the reporting lines and safeguards for the Head of Internal Audit and Head of Compliance
Build the compliance risk management cycle: CRA, monitoring plan, change management, approvals and reporting
Design a mandatory, role-based compliance training programme that meets section 5.4.3

cards.title: A new rulebook with a deadline
cards.setting: Compliance Division, Krishnachura Bank PLC, the week the July 2026 circular arrived.

lines.text: BRPD-2 Circular 03 is out. The 2016 internal control and compliance guidelines are repealed, and we must restructure by 31 December 2026.
Habibur Rahman, Head of HR and Training. I saw section 5.4.3. Compliance and HR must jointly run a mandatory, role-based compliance training programme. That's us.
And my audit committee now gets a quarterly compliance report from Mitali, plus closure confirmations on every high-risk audit finding.
Three gates to pass: who owns risk, who checks it and who gives independent assurance. Then the training programme.
Where do we even start?
With the compliance risk assessment. Everything else, the training included, is built on it.

cards.title: Three lines of defence, the 2026 way

scenes.heading: First line: business units
scenes.narration: Branches and business units own their compliance risks. They run the controls and follow internal policies and external rules in daily work.

scenes.heading: Second line: compliance and risk
scenes.narration: The compliance function gives independent oversight, challenge and expertise. It builds the compliance risk framework, policies and tools and tests whether first-line controls work.

scenes.heading: Third line: internal audit
scenes.narration: Internal audit gives independent, objective assurance to the board and its audit committee on governance, risk management and internal control, including the first two lines.

scenes.heading: Formal adoption
scenes.narration: The guidelines say banks must formally adopt and implement the three lines model so that accountability is clear.

items.label: Business units
items.detail: First line: own the risks and run the controls.

items.label: Head of Compliance
items.detail: Reports to the audit committee through the MD/CEO; may speak freely to the committee or board.

items.label: Head of Internal Audit
items.detail: Reports directly to the audit committee, which also appraises the role.

items.label: Audit committee of the board
items.detail: Reviews the compliance report at least quarterly.

items.label: Board of directors
items.detail: Sets the tone from the top; reviews internal control effectiveness at least yearly.

cards.question: A Krishnachura branch manager says 'compliance is the Compliance Division's job, not mine'. How do the 2026 guidelines answer?
options: Business units are the first line: they own and manage the compliance risks in their own activities
Correct: the second line carries all compliance responsibility
Correct, unless internal audit finds a breach at the branch
Branches share it only with internal audit, the third line
cards.explanation: Section 1.4 makes management and staff in business units directly responsible for identifying, assessing and managing compliance risks and for executing controls.

cards.title: Safeguards for the two heads
cards.body:
Section 2.3 of the guidelines protects the independence of the Head of Internal Audit (HoIA) and Head of Compliance (HoC):

- Both have a **charter** approved by the audit committee and the board.
- The HoIA reports **directly to the audit committee**, which appraises him or her; complaints against the HoIA go to the committee through the MD/CEO.
- The HoC reports to the committee **through the MD/CEO** but may disclose findings freely to the committee or board; the MD/CEO appraises the HoC.
- Both should ideally be **no lower than two steps below the CEO**, hold the **same designation** and have **no other duties**.
- ICMS staff have **unrestricted access** to records and people; no one punished for a major offence or under disciplinary proceedings may be posted there; auditors never audit their own past work.
- ICMS staff take a **planned, confidential 10-day mandatory leave** each year.
- The appointment, transfer or removal of the HoIA and HoC needs the **audit committee's approval**.

cards.title: Match the ICMS role to its duty
cards.prompt: Each pairing comes from the July 2026 guidelines.

pairs.right: Maintains the compliance charter, annual CRA and risk-based monitoring plan
Confirms closure of critical or high-risk observations and reports it to the audit committee
Certifies yearly to the board how effective internal control has been
Reviews the Head of Compliance's comprehensive report at least quarterly
Sets a tone from the top that promotes honesty, integrity and compliance
Develop and deliver the mandatory, role-based compliance training programme

cards.title: The compliance risk management cycle

items.label: Compliance risk assessment
items.detail: Bank-wide, at least yearly: inherent risk, control strength, residual risk.

items.label: Monitoring plan
items.detail: Risk-based reviews testing key controls, drawn from the CRA.

items.label: Change and approvals
items.detail: Track new rules; compliance approves new products in writing before launch.

items.label: Training and awareness
items.detail: Mandatory, role-based, built on the CRA; effectiveness measured.

items.label: Reporting
items.detail: HoC reports to the audit committee and senior management at least quarterly.

cards.caption: Sections 5.3-5.4. Findings feed the next year's assessment.

cards.title: What does 'role-based' mean?
cards.setting: HR and Training Division meeting room.

lines.text: Easy option: one e-learning module for all 4,000 staff, once a year, done.
That isn't role-based, and it isn't built on our compliance risk assessment. Our CRA says trade finance and lending carry most of our compliance risk.
My tellers need different things from my credit officers. And nobody has ever checked if the training changed anything at Agrabad.
So we need different paths by role, tied to the risks, and a way to measure effectiveness.
And we report the results. The guideline says the effectiveness must be measured and reported.

cards.title: Designing the programme
cards.situation: Krishnachura must meet section 5.4.3 of the ICMS guidelines before the 31 December 2026 deadline. The training budget allows either one generic annual e-learning course for all staff, or a smaller set of role-based modules with assessments. The CRA ranks trade finance, credit and branch cash operations as the highest compliance risks.

choices.text: Build role-based paths from the CRA (trade, credit, branch operations, ICMS staff, managers), make them mandatory, test learners and report completion and results to senior management and the audit committee.
choices.outcome: Best. This meets every element of section 5.4.3: compliance and HR together, mandatory, role-based, CRA-based curriculum, and measured and reported effectiveness.

choices.text: Run the generic e-learning course for everyone and add role-based modules next year.
choices.outcome: Partly right. A common baseline helps, but on its own it is not role-based or built on the CRA, so it would not meet the guideline by the deadline.

choices.text: Let each division head choose whatever training they like and report attendance.
choices.outcome: Poor. The guideline puts the programme on compliance and HR, and attendance alone is not a measure of effectiveness.

choices.text: Train only the Compliance Division, since compliance is the second line's job.
choices.outcome: Poor. The first line owns compliance risk; leaving branches and business units untrained ignores the three lines model.

cards.title: Head of Internal Audit and Head of Compliance

items.label: Reports to
items.right: Audit committee through the MD/CEO, with free access

items.label: Charter
items.left: Internal audit charter approved by committee and board
items.right: Compliance policy charter approved by committee and board

items.label: Shared rules
items.left: Same designation; ideally within two steps of the CEO
items.right: No other duties; moves need audit committee approval

cards.caption: Sections 2.3.1 to 2.3.3 of the July 2026 ICMS guidelines.

cards.title: Closing an audit observation
cards.prompt: Put the steps in the order section 5.5 requires.
steps: The Head of Compliance logs the observation in the central register with an ID, risk rating, owner and target date
Management designs a SMART corrective action and reports progress to compliance
Compliance reviews evidence and talks to the process owner when management reports it closed
Internal audit re-tests the control to validate the fix
For a critical or high-risk observation, the Head of Internal Audit confirms closure and reports it to the audit committee

cards.question: Branch operations says an inspection finding is 'closed' because a new procedure was issued. When may it be treated as closed?
options: When the action is implemented, internal audit's re-test confirms the risk is mitigated and no significant residual risk remains
When the branch manager signs the closure form
When the new procedure has been emailed to all branches
When ninety days have passed with no repeat finding
cards.explanation: Section 5.5(e) sets three closure criteria; for critical or high-risk items the Head of Internal Audit must also confirm closure and report it to the audit committee.

cards.title: Real case: Bangladesh Bank moves to risk-based supervision (2026)
cards.body:
Bangladesh Bank's Monetary Policy Statement for January-June 2026 says it implemented **risk-based supervision (RBS) from 4 January 2026**, to strengthen forward-looking risk assessment, risk governance and accountability. It reports that **more than 500 of its officials** were trained in RBS. The same statement notes new rules that bar banks from paying dividends while short of capital or provisions, and from paying staff bonuses unless the bank makes a profit under proper accounting.

The July 2026 ICMS guidelines say they were written to support the move to RBS. Under RBS, supervisors look at **how well a bank finds and controls its own risks**. A bank with a real CRA, a working monitoring plan and training that changes behaviour is far better placed than one that only collects attendance sheets.

cards.title: Evidence that training works
cards.body:
Section 5.4.3 asks for effectiveness to be **measured and reported**. Useful measures:

- Completion by role and deadline, with escalation of overdue staff.
- Pass rates on scenario-based tests, not just attendance.
- Trends in audit and inspection findings in the trained areas.
- Repeat findings, which show where training did not change practice.

Put these in the Head of Compliance's quarterly report to the audit committee.

cards.title: Stage 3 take-aways
items: The 2026 ICMS guidelines replace the 2016 ICC guidelines; banks must restructure by 31 December 2026.
Business units are the first line, compliance and risk the second, internal audit the third.
The HoIA reports directly to the audit committee; the HoC reports through the MD/CEO with free access to the committee.
A bank-wide compliance risk assessment at least yearly drives the monitoring plan and the training curriculum.
Compliance and HR must run mandatory, role-based compliance training and measure and report its effectiveness.

cards.prompt: Which compliance risks in your own role would a role-based programme need to cover? How would you show, with evidence, that the training changed what you do?

quiz.question: Under the July 2026 ICMS guidelines, who forms the first line of defence?
options: The compliance function
Internal audit
Management and staff in the business units
The audit committee of the board
quiz.explanation: Section 1.4 says business units own and are directly responsible for managing the compliance risks in their activities and for running controls.

quiz.question: By what date must banks restructure to meet the 2026 ICMS guidelines?
options: 30 June 2026
31 December 2026
31 March 2027
21 July 2027
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 3 of BRPD-2 Circular 03 of 21 July 2026 requires banks to complete the restructuring needed to align with ICMS by 31 December 2026.

quiz.question: To whom does the Head of Internal Audit report under the 2026 guidelines?
options: To the MD/CEO, who appraises the role
To the Head of Compliance
To the chair of the board in person
Directly to the audit committee of the board
quiz.explanation: Section 2.3.1.6 says the HoIA reports activities and findings directly to the audit committee and has full and free access to it; the committee also carries out the appraisal.

quiz.question: What does section 5.4.3 of the ICMS guidelines require?
options: Every employee must pass an external compliance certificate within one year
HR must run one compliance course a year for all staff together, with attendance reported to the board
Internal audit must design and deliver compliance training to branches
Mandatory, role-based compliance training by compliance and HR, built on the CRA and measured
quiz.explanation: Section 5.4.3 puts the programme on the compliance function together with HR, makes it mandatory and role-based, ties the curriculum to the CRA and requires its effectiveness to be measured and reported.

quiz.question: How often must a bank carry out its bank-wide compliance risk assessment?
options: At least once every three years
At least once a year
Only before a Bangladesh Bank inspection
At least once a month
quiz.explanation: Section 5.3.4.2 requires a bank-wide CRA at least annually, which then informs the compliance monitoring plan.

quiz.question: Krishnachura plans to launch a new digital loan product next month. What must happen first under section 5.4.2?
options: The audit committee must approve the product's pricing
Internal audit must audit the first 100 loans
The compliance function must be consulted and give written approval before launch
Bangladesh Bank must approve the product in writing before any customer can apply for it
quiz.explanation: Section 5.4.2 requires compliance to be consulted and give written approval on all new products, processes and major initiatives before launch.

quiz.question: Which officer may NOT be posted to the ICMS under the 2026 guidelines?
options: An officer currently under disciplinary proceedings
An officer with an accounting degree
An officer who previously worked in a branch
An officer who joined less than three years ago
quiz.explanation: Section 2.3.3.5 says people punished for a major offence and people under disciplinary proceedings must not be posted to ICMS; track records must be checked first.

quiz.question: How often must the Head of Compliance report to the audit committee and senior management?
options: At least yearly
At least quarterly
At least monthly
Only when a significant breach occurs
quiz.explanation: Section 5.4.4 requires comprehensive reports at least quarterly; significant breaches must also be reported immediately under section 5.3.3.6.

quiz.question: An internal audit team finds an irregularity involving the MD/CEO. Under section 2.7, where must it be reported?
options: To the MD/CEO first, so that he can respond
Only to the shareholders at the next AGM
To the bank's external auditor, who then decides whether to inform Bangladesh Bank or the full board
Confidentially and directly to BRPD-2 and the relevant supervision department of Bangladesh Bank
quiz.explanation: Section 2.7 says irregularities found against the board or MD/CEO during an audit are communicated confidentially and directly to Bangladesh Bank's BRPD-2 and the concerned bank supervision department.

quiz.question: Krishnachura's HR head proposes measuring the new compliance training by attendance only. What is the strongest objection?
options: Section 5.4.3 asks for measured effectiveness; attendance shows presence, not learning
Attendance records may not be kept for long under the new personal data protection law of 2026
Bangladesh Bank sets a fixed pass mark that attendance cannot meet
Training records belong to internal audit, not HR
quiz.explanation: The guideline asks for effectiveness to be measured and reported. Test results, audit trends and repeat findings show impact; attendance only shows presence.

sessions.title: The Code of Conduct, Ethics and the Whistleblower Framework
sessions.summary: Apply Bangladesh Bank's Code of Conduct for banks to gifts, conflicts, outside work, inside information and confidentiality, see how a bank adopts and embeds its own code, and use the mandatory whistleblower framework in section 8.4 of the 2026 ICMS guidelines and the Public Interest Information Disclosure Act 2011.
objectives: Apply the Code's rules on use of position, conflicts of interest, gifts, outside employment and insider trading
Explain how a bank adopts, circulates, signs off and enforces its own code of conduct
Use the whistleblower framework: who can report, what, through which channels and with what protection
Explain the protection the Public Interest Information Disclosure Act 2011 gives to people who report

cards.title: A gift basket and a quiet warning
cards.setting: Agrabad branch, Chattogram, the week before Eid.

lines.text: A large gift hamper has arrived for my credit officer from a garments customer whose limit renewal is on his desk.
The Code is clear: no gift that puts you under an obligation to the giver, without the competent authority's permission. Anything delivered by courier goes straight to a senior for disposal.
There's more. One of my officers says a colleague has been splitting cash deposits for that same customer. She's afraid to say it openly.
Then she needs the whistleblower channel, and she needs to know she is protected.
Most staff signed the code on their first day and never looked at it again.
Stage four: the Integrity Bridge. Let's make the code something people use.

scenes.heading: One code for the industry
scenes.narration: In 2017 Bangladesh Bank issued a Code of Conduct for banks and non-bank financial institutions, as a minimum standard for directors, staff and others who deal with them.

scenes.heading: Every bank builds its own
scenes.narration: Each bank must develop its own code in line with it and circulate it formally within sixty days, with the board and management responsible for putting it into practice.

scenes.heading: Everyone signs
scenes.narration: New and existing employees commit to the code and sign a statement of compliance.

scenes.heading: Training and culture
scenes.narration: Banks must train staff to act with integrity and hold seminars and workshops on ethics and compliance. An ethics committee runs a yearly work plan.

scenes.heading: Fair discipline
scenes.narration: Breaches go through a written disciplinary procedure that is fair, consistent and proportionate.

items.label: Board adopts
items.detail: BRPD 02/2024 para 10: code of conduct and ethics for all staff.

items.label: Circulate and sign
items.detail: Formal circulation within 60 days; statement of compliance from each employee.

items.label: Train
items.detail: Induction, foundation training and ethics workshops (Code s.4.2, s.32).

items.label: Speak up
items.detail: Channels and protection under the ICMS whistleblower framework.

items.label: Monitor and discipline
items.detail: Ethics committee work plan; fair disciplinary procedure.

cards.question: A customer offers Krishnachura's credit officer an expensive phone after a loan is approved. Under the Code, what should he do?
options: Decline it, or if it arrives anyway, hand it to his superior for disposal and report it
Keep it, because the loan was already approved
Keep it if its value is declared in his annual asset statement
Give it to a family member so it is not a gift to him
cards.explanation: Section 12 of the Code bars accepting gifts, personally or through family, that create an obligation to the giver without permission; items sent by post or courier are handed to higher authority for disposal. Section 8.2(j) also forbids gifts from people who benefit from the employee's office.

cards.title: Conflicts, outside work and inside information
cards.body:
Key duties in the Code (sections 7-13 and 31):

- **Use of position (s.7):** using your post for private gain, or to favour your own people, is treated as abuse of power and corruption.
- **Conflicts (s.8):** avoid any undue benefit for yourself, family or relatives; do not trade, hold business stakes or advise others in ways that harm the bank.
- **Outside work (ss.9-10):** no other trade or job without the competent authority's prior permission; honorary social or charitable work is allowed if duties do not suffer.
- **Political pressure (s.11):** never use a member of parliament, politician or director to win a posting, promotion or transfer.
- **Suppliers (s.13):** disclose personal links with a vendor to top management before negotiations.
- **Insider trading (s.31):** never trade, or tip others, on price-sensitive non-public information, including about your own bank.
- **Confidentiality (ss.6, 27, 36):** customer information stays secret unless a court or lawful authority requires it, during and after employment.

cards.title: Allowed, needs permission or prohibited?
cards.prompt: Sort each situation using Bangladesh Bank's Code of Conduct.

items.text: Volunteering on weekends at a local charity school
Taking a paid evening job as a consultant to an accounting firm
Negotiating a contract with a printing firm owned by your cousin
Asking a director to help you get transferred to Dhaka
Buying your bank's shares after hearing unpublished quarterly results
Speaking to a newspaper about the bank's loan losses
Accepting a foreign award or title
Sharing a customer's balance with his brother who asks politely

cards.title: Whistleblower framework (ICMS 8.4)

items.label: Who is covered
items.detail: All staff incl. contractual and temporary, the board, senior management, customers, vendors and agents.

items.label: What can be reported
items.detail: Fraud, bribery, false records, policy or code breaches, regulatory or ESG non-compliance, retaliation.

items.label: How
items.detail: Email or hotline, secure online system, or a sealed confidential letter to the HoC or audit committee chair.

items.label: Protection
items.detail: Identity kept confidential; anonymous reports accepted; no demotion, suspension or harassment.

items.label: Investigation
items.detail: Register, assess, refer for full investigation, report findings to the audit committee chair.

cards.caption: Section 5.3.3.3 also requires the mechanism to work effectively and free of retaliation.

cards.title: The officer who wants to speak up
cards.setting: A quiet meeting room at the Agrabad branch.

lines.text: Junior officer Tania has seen a colleague break a large cash deposit into smaller amounts across several days for the same customer.
Tania is frightened. The colleague is popular, and she worries her appraisal will suffer.
She can report through the hotline or in a sealed envelope marked as a confidential whistleblower report to me or the audit committee chair. She can even stay anonymous if she gives enough detail.
And if she's wrong?
If she reported in good faith, she is protected even if the allegation is not proved. And because it looks like structuring, the AML team must also look at it.

cards.title: Handling a whistleblower report
cards.situation: A confidential letter reaches Krishnachura's Head of Compliance alleging that the Agrabad cash officer splits a customer's deposits to avoid reporting. The branch manager, who received a copy, wants to call the cash officer in, read him the letter and ask who wrote it 'to clear the air'.

choices.text: Register and acknowledge the report, keep the reporter's identity strictly need-to-know, do a preliminary assessment, refer it for investigation and alert the AML team without tipping off the customer.
choices.outcome: Best. This follows sections 8.4.3-8.4.5: confidentiality, assessment, referral and findings to the audit committee chair. Possible structuring also triggers the bank's AML escalation.

choices.text: Let the branch manager hold the meeting but ask him not to name the reporter.
choices.outcome: Poor. Reading the letter to the subject risks revealing the reporter and tipping off the customer, and it bypasses the investigation process.

choices.text: Wait to see if more letters arrive before acting.
choices.outcome: Poor. The framework requires a report to be registered and assessed; delay can let wrongdoing and evidence loss continue.

choices.text: Pass the letter to the cash officer's line manager to investigate quietly.
choices.outcome: Partly right in that someone acts, but the line manager is too close; the guidelines route cases to the assigned auditor, team or division, with findings to the audit committee chair.

cards.title: Protection for people who speak up

cards.back: Under ICMS 8.4.3 the whistleblower's identity is kept strictly confidential and case files are handled on a need-to-know basis.
They must be taken up if they contain enough information to investigate.
Protection still applies if the allegation turns out unsubstantiated, as long as it was made in good faith.
No demotion, suspension or harassment. Bangladesh Bank may act against a bank that retaliates, and credible reports may be rewarded.
A person who discloses public-interest information to an appropriate authority is protected from criminal, civil and departmental cases for that disclosure.
An employee who discloses may not be demoted, given a harassing transfer, forced to retire or treated in a discriminatory way because of it.

cards.title: Code and ethics numbers to remember

items.label: Days to circulate the bank's code
items.detail: Code of Conduct s.37: formal circulation after adoption.

items.label: Ethics committee work plan
items.detail: Plan each year and monitor progress against it (s.37).

items.label: Staff who sign the code
items.detail: New and existing employees sign a statement of compliance (s.40).

items.label: Whistleblower channels
items.detail: Email/hotline, online system, sealed confidential letter (ICMS 8.4.2).

cards.question: Which of these does the ICMS whistleblower framework NOT list among the people it covers?
options: Members of the public with no dealings with the bank
Contractual and temporary staff
Members of the board and senior management
Vendors and agents with official dealings with the bank
cards.explanation: Section 8.4 covers all employees (permanent, contractual, temporary), the board and senior management, and external stakeholders such as customers, vendors, consultants and agents with official dealings with the bank.

cards.title: Building Krishnachura's speak-up line
cards.body:
Mitali's team sets up the framework in four weeks:

- A **dedicated email and hotline** answered by the issue handling unit, plus a page on the intranet for secure online reports.
- A notice in every branch on sending a **sealed letter marked 'Confidential Whistleblower Report'** to the Head of Compliance or the audit committee chair.
- A **case register** with access limited to two named officers; files stored securely, need-to-know only.
- A rule that any report naming the MD/CEO or a director goes to the **audit committee chair**, and that audit irregularities against the board or MD/CEO go confidentially to Bangladesh Bank under section 2.7.
- A one-page **'how we protect you'** note covering anonymity, good faith and no retaliation.
- Quarterly **statistics** (number, type, age, outcome) in the compliance report, without names.

cards.title: Speak up early
cards.body: The Code says that if fraud, theft or illegal activity comes to your notice you must report it at once to your superior or management, acting as a whistleblower (s.16). If the concern involves your own superior, use the confidential channels instead. Write down what you saw, when and where, but do not investigate on your own or confront the person.

cards.title: Stage 4 take-aways
items: Bangladesh Bank's 2017 Code is a minimum standard; each bank adopts its own code and circulates it within 60 days.
Every employee signs a statement of compliance; the board and management are responsible for implementation.
No obligating gifts, no use of position for private gain, no outside work without permission, no insider trading.
The ICMS whistleblower framework covers staff, directors and external parties, with confidential and anonymous channels.
Good-faith reporters are protected from retaliation, and the PID Act 2011 adds legal protection for public-interest disclosures.

cards.prompt: If you saw a colleague break the code tomorrow, which channel would you use at your bank, and what would make you confident you were protected?

quiz.question: Within how many days must a bank formally circulate its own code of conduct developed in line with Bangladesh Bank's Code?
options: 30 days
90 days
180 days
60 days
quiz.explanation: Section 37(i) of the Code of Conduct for Banks and NBFIs requires formal circulation within 60 days.

quiz.question: Which body does BRPD Circular 02/2024 make responsible for adopting a code of conduct and code of ethics for all bank staff?
options: The Head of Compliance
The board of directors
The Ethics Committee of Bangladesh Bank
The Bangladesh Association of Banks
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 10.1(d) of BRPD Circular 02/2024 requires the board to formulate an integrity policy, code of conduct and code of ethics for all staff and to set high ethical standards.

quiz.question: A courier delivers an expensive watch from a customer to a relationship manager's desk. What does the Code require?
options: Return it to the customer by courier without telling anyone
Keep it if its value is below the bank's gift threshold
Receive it but hand it over immediately to higher authority for disposal
Donate it to a charity in the bank's name on the same day and tell the customer afterwards
quiz.explanation: Section 12(i) of the Code says gifts sent by post or courier may be received but must immediately be handed to higher authority for disposal.

quiz.question: What must every new and existing employee do under section 40 of the Code?
options: Commit to the code and sign a statement of compliance
Pass a written ethics exam every year
Declare all relatives working in other banks
Attend a seminar organised by Bangladesh Bank
quiz.explanation: Section 40(i) requires all new and existing employees to commit to the code of conduct and sign a statement attesting compliance.

quiz.question: An officer hears unpublished quarterly results and tells his brother to buy the bank's shares. Which part of the Code does this breach?
options: The rules on outside employment
The ban on insider trading, which includes tipping others
The dress code and grooming standards
The rules on media interaction
quiz.explanation: Section 31 prohibits trading on material non-public information and expressly covers giving tips or encouraging others to deal.

quiz.question: Which of these is a reportable issue under ICMS section 8.4.1?
options: A disagreement about annual leave dates
A customer's complaint about ATM downtime
A dispute between two branches over targets
Retaliation or harassment against a whistleblower
quiz.explanation: Section 8.4.1 lists fraud, bribery, record manipulation, breaches of policy or the code, regulatory or ESG non-compliance, and retaliation or harassment against any whistleblower.

quiz.question: Krishnachura receives an anonymous whistleblower email with dates, account numbers and names. What does the framework say?
options: It must be taken up, because it contains enough information to investigate
It must be ignored until the sender identifies himself
It may be taken up only after two named witnesses confirm the facts in writing to compliance
It must be forwarded to the police before any review
quiz.explanation: Section 8.4.3 says anonymous complaints shall be entertained if they contain adequate information for investigation.

quiz.question: A whistleblower's allegation is investigated and not proved. She reported honestly. What protection does she keep?
options: None, since the allegation was unsubstantiated
Protection only if she apologises to the person named
Full protection, because the report was made in good faith
Protection only for the first report she makes
quiz.explanation: Section 8.4.4 says protection extends even if the allegation is unsubstantiated, provided it was made in good faith.

quiz.question: Under the Public Interest Information Disclosure Act 2011, what may NOT be done to an employee because she disclosed public-interest information to an appropriate authority?
options: Asking her to support her disclosure with documents
Keeping her identity confidential without her consent
Demotion, a harassing transfer or forced retirement
Recording the disclosure in writing
quiz.explanation: Section 5(3) of the Act bars demotion, harassing transfer, compulsory retirement, departmental action or discrimination because of the disclosure. Section 4 expects supporting documents where available.

quiz.question: A relationship manager's brother-in-law owns a firm bidding for the bank's printing contract, and she sits on the evaluation panel. What should she do?
options: Disclose the relationship to top management before negotiations and step away from the decision
Stay on the panel but score the firm slightly lower to be fair
Say nothing, since a brother-in-law is not close family
Ask the firm quietly to withdraw from the tender so that the conflict disappears before anyone notices
quiz.explanation: Section 13 of the Code requires personal relationships with contractors and vendors to be disclosed to top management when negotiations begin, and they must not influence decisions; section 8 requires conflicts to be avoided.

sessions.title: Harassment Prevention, Foundation Training and Inspection Readiness
sessions.summary: Apply the Labour (Amendment) Act 2026: the new definition of sexual harassment, the employer duties in the new section 332 (policy, risk assessment, information and training) and the complaints committee in section 332A; then bring the programme together with the 2026 foundation training rules and the evidence Bangladesh Bank will expect.
objectives: Recognise conduct the Labour Act 2026 defines as sexual harassment, including quid pro quo and hostile environment
List the employer duties in the new section 332, including information and training for workers
Set up a complaints committee that meets section 332A
Apply BRPD-1 Circular 10 of 2026 on foundation training and assemble the evidence of a complete programme

cards.title: A complaint with nowhere to go
cards.setting: HR and Training Division, Krishnachura Bank PLC, Motijheel.

lines.text: A trainee officer at Sylhet says a senior officer keeps sending her messages with sexual jokes and told her a good evaluation 'depends on being friendly'.
She called me because I was her mentor in Agrabad. She doesn't know who to complain to in Sylhet.
Since April the Labour Act puts specific duties on us as an employer: a workplace policy, risk assessment, training and a complaints committee.
Our old committee had three men and one woman from HR.
Then it no longer fits the law. Stage five: the Safe Workplace Summit. Then we pull the whole programme together for the inspectors.

scenes.heading: A new definition
scenes.narration: The Labour (Amendment) Act 2026 adds a legal definition of sexual harassment to the Labour Act. It covers unwelcome sexual conduct, quid pro quo demands and conduct that creates a hostile or humiliating workplace.

scenes.heading: Banks are covered
scenes.narration: The Labour Act lists banks among commercial establishments, so a bank as employer carries these duties.

scenes.heading: A new section 332
scenes.narration: Employers must prevent violence and harassment, publicise the prohibitions and penalties, adopt a workplace policy, assess the risks and give workers information and training.

scenes.heading: A new section 332A
scenes.narration: Every employer forms a five-member complaints committee, led by a woman, with a female majority from within and two members from outside organisations working on gender and sexual violence.

scenes.heading: The Code already agreed
scenes.narration: Bangladesh Bank's Code of Conduct also requires banks to keep the workplace free from harassment and not to tolerate it from directors, managers or staff.

cards.title: Employer duties under the new section 332(1)

items.label: Keep the workplace safe
items.detail: Ensure the work environment is not hostile; prevent violence and harassment.

items.label: Publicise
items.detail: Make the prohibitions and penalties widely known.

items.label: Policy
items.detail: Adopt and apply a workplace policy against violence and harassment.

items.label: Assess risk
items.detail: Identify and assess the risks, including psychosocial risks, and control them.

items.label: Inform and train
items.detail: Give workers information and training on risks, protection, rights and duties.

items.label: Publish and support
items.detail: Describe complaint handling on the website; help pursue legal action.

cards.question: Which of these does the 2026 definition of sexual harassment include?
options: Linking a job decision, such as an evaluation, to accepting or rejecting sexual conduct
A manager's fair criticism of an officer's work in a private meeting
A one-off disagreement between colleagues about branch targets
An HR officer asking about leave plans for a rota
cards.explanation: The new definition covers 'quid pro quo' harassment, where accepting or rejecting sexual conduct is used to influence a job decision, as well as conduct that creates a hostile or humiliating work environment.

cards.title: The complaints committee under section 332A
cards.body:
Every employer must form a **complaints committee on discrimination, violence and harassment**:

- **Five members**.
- A **majority of women** drawn from within the establishment.
- **Headed by a woman**.
- **Two members from organisations** that work on gender and sexual violence.

How it works:

- It receives, investigates and handles every complaint or related report, following **zero tolerance** for discrimination, violence and harassment.
- It acts with **confidentiality and respect for human dignity** and must not obstruct a complaint.
- After a **written complaint**, it acts in the way the rules under the Act set out.

Section 332(2) adds that no colleague or anyone else may behave towards a woman at work in a way that is obscene, indecent or against her dignity, whatever her rank.

cards.title: Harassment examples and the rule they meet
cards.prompt: Match each behaviour or duty to the 2026 provision it relates to.

pairs.left: Repeated sexual jokes by text message

pairs.right: Quid pro quo harassment in the definition

pairs.left: No complaint procedure on the bank's website
Committee of three men and one woman
pairs.right: Breaches the composition rule in section 332A

pairs.left: No harassment module in staff training
pairs.right: Duty to give information and training in section 332(1)

items.label: Committee members
items.detail: Fixed size of the complaints committee.

items.label: Committee head
items.detail: The committee must be led by a woman.

items.label: External members
items.detail: From organisations working on gender and sexual violence.

items.label: Women from within
items.detail: Must form the majority of the committee.

cards.title: The trainee's choice
cards.setting: Video call between Sylhet and Dhaka.

lines.text: The trainee officer is in week nine of her fourteen-week foundation course, doing practical training at the Sylhet branch.
Her supervisor writes part of her practical assessment. She worries a complaint will cost her the Foundation Training Certificate, and with it her confirmation.
She also asked if she could just change branches quietly.
She can ask for that, but moving her alone puts the burden on the person who complained. The committee should handle it, and her assessment must be protected.
So what do we do today?

cards.title: Responding to the trainee's complaint
cards.situation: A trainee officer at Krishnachura's Sylhet branch says her supervisor sends sexual jokes and hinted her evaluation depends on 'being friendly'.
