Completing foundation training is required for her confirmation, and the supervisor writes part of her assessment. Krishnachura has just rebuilt its complaints committee to meet section 332A.

choices.text: Take her written complaint to the complaints committee, keep it confidential, have another officer assess her practical training meanwhile, and keep the screenshots and messages as evidence.
choices.outcome: Best. The committee investigates under section 332A with confidentiality and zero tolerance, and removing the supervisor from her assessment protects her from quid pro quo pressure.

choices.text: Move the trainee to another branch at once and close the matter without a complaint.
choices.outcome: Poor. It burdens the complainant, leaves the behaviour unexamined and ignores the employer's duty to prevent harassment.

choices.text: Ask the branch manager to speak informally to the supervisor and report back.
choices.outcome: Partly right. Quick action matters, but an informal chat is no substitute for the committee, and it may expose her before the case is handled properly.

choices.text: Wait until her foundation course ends so her certificate is not put at risk.
choices.outcome: Poor. Delay leaves her exposed for weeks and lets the supervisor keep shaping her assessment.

items.label: Who
items.left: All newly recruited officers, by any title
items.right: Promoted officers who never had foundation training

items.label: Length
items.right: At least 8 weeks theory and 6 weeks practice

items.label: Legal and ethics content
items.left: Bank Company Act, MLPA and other banking laws
items.right: The bank's code of conduct, ethics and integrity

items.label: Policy
items.right: Guidelines are a minimum; banks may go further

items.label: Outcome
items.right: Completion required for confirmation in service

cards.title: Assembling the evidence pack for 31 December
cards.prompt: Put Krishnachura's readiness steps in a sensible order.
steps: Complete the bank-wide compliance risk assessment
Map each role to its required training: board, senior managers, ICMS staff, new officers, branches
Adopt board-approved policies: code of conduct, whistleblowing, harassment and training
Deliver the role-based modules, foundation course and harassment training
Measure results: completion, test scores, audit and inspection trends
Report results to senior management and the audit committee and keep the records

cards.question: A new probationary officer has finished 10 weeks of classroom training and 2 weeks at a branch. Can the bank confirm her in service now?
options: No: she needs at least 14 weeks in total, with at least 6 weeks of practical training
Yes: 12 weeks is enough if she passed all her tests
Yes: the 14-week figure is only a recommendation
No: she must also work two years before confirmation
cards.explanation: BRPD-1 Circular 10 sets a minimum of 14 weeks, with at least 8 weeks of theory and 6 weeks of practice, and makes completion mandatory for confirmation of service.

cards.title: Krishnachura's training map, December 2026
cards.body:
Mitali and Habib finish the year with one table the inspectors can follow:

| Audience | Training | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Directors | Induction on banking law and duties | BRPD 02/2024 para 14 (may be arranged) |
| All staff by role | Role-based compliance modules with tests | ICMS 5.4.3 (mandatory) |
| ICMS staff | Advanced local and foreign training | ICMS 2.3.3.11 |
| New officers | 14-week foundation course incl. code and ethics | BRPD-1 Circ. 10/2026 |
| All workers | Violence and harassment risks, rights, duties | Labour Act s.332 (2026) |
| All staff | Ethics workshops; signed code | Code of Conduct ss.32, 40 |

Each line has an owner, a schedule, completion data and a quarterly report line.

cards.title: Make harassment training real
cards.body: Use short scenarios set in your own branches: messages after hours, comments at a training centre, pressure linked to evaluations. Tell people exactly **who sits on the committee, how to complain in writing and how confidentiality works**. Train managers separately on how to respond on day one without investigating alone or blaming the complainant.

cards.title: Stage 5 take-aways
items: The Labour Act now defines sexual harassment, including quid pro quo and hostile-environment conduct.
Under the new section 332, employers adopt a policy, assess risks and give workers information and training.
Section 332A requires a five-member complaints committee led by a woman, with a female majority and two outside members.
Foundation training lasts at least 14 weeks (8 theory, 6 practice) and is required for confirmation.
A ready bank can show its CRA, role map, policies, delivery records, results and reports to the audit committee.

cards.prompt: Who would you contact today if you faced harassment at work? If you do not know the answer, what does that tell you about your bank's programme?

quiz.question: Which Act added a legal definition of sexual harassment to the Bangladesh Labour Act 2006?
options: The Bangladesh Labour (Amendment) Act 2026
The Bank Company (Amendment) Act 2023
The Public Interest Information Disclosure Act 2011
The Personal Data Protection Act 2026
quiz.explanation: Act No. 43 of 2026, dated 10 April 2026, inserted a new definition of sexual harassment as section 2(52A) of the Labour Act.

quiz.question: How many members must the complaints committee under the new section 332A have?
options: Three
Five
Seven
Nine
quiz.explanation: Section 332A(1) requires a five-member committee.

quiz.question: Who must head the complaints committee under section 332A?
options: The head of HR
The managing director
A member from an outside organisation
A woman
quiz.explanation: Section 332A(1) requires the committee to be headed by a woman, with a female majority from within the establishment.

quiz.question: How many members of the section 332A committee must come from organisations working on gender and sexual violence?
options: Two
One
Three
None, all must be employees
quiz.explanation: Section 332A(1) requires two members from organisations that work on gender and sexual abuse.

quiz.question: Which of these is an employer duty under the new section 332(1)?
options: Paying every complainant a fixed compensation within one month
Reporting every complaint and its outcome to Bangladesh Bank within seven days of receipt
Informing and training workers on harassment risks, protection, rights and duties
Requiring complainants to bring two witnesses before acting
quiz.explanation: Section 332(1)(g) requires information and training on identified risks and hazards, prevention and protection measures, and workers' rights and duties.

quiz.question: Why do the Labour Act's harassment duties apply to a bank?
options: Bangladesh Bank adopted the Labour Act as a circular
Only state-owned banks are covered, as public bodies
Banks are listed as commercial establishments under the Labour Act
The duties apply only if the bank has a trade union
quiz.explanation: Section 2 of the Labour Act 2006 lists banks and banking companies among commercial establishments, so employer duties reach them.

quiz.question: What is the minimum length of foundation training for newly recruited officers under BRPD-1 Circular 10 of 2026?
options: 14 weeks: at least 8 of theory and 6 of practice
10 weeks: at least 6 of theory and 4 of practice
6 months of classroom training only
4 weeks of induction plus 1 year on the job
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 4 of the guidelines sets a minimum total of 14 weeks, with at least 8 weeks of theoretical and 6 weeks of practical training.

quiz.question: Which legal and regulatory topics must foundation training cover at a minimum?
options: Only the bank's product manuals and sales targets
Only international standards such as the Basel framework and the FATF Recommendations
Only the Labour Act and the Companies Act
Major banking laws and the bank's own code of conduct, staff rules and ethics
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 5(E) lists major banking laws (including the Bank Company Act and MLPA) and Bangladesh Bank circulars, the bank's code of conduct, staff regulations and HR policy, its risk management guidelines, and ethics and professional integrity.

quiz.question: An officer was promoted into an officer grade but never attended foundation training. What does BRPD-1 Circular 10 require?
options: Nothing, because he is not newly recruited
The bank must make sure he takes part in foundation training
He must resign and be re-recruited
He must pass a Bangladesh Bank exam instead
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 3 says that for officials promoted to equivalent positions who have not had foundation training, banks shall ensure their participation.

quiz.question: A supervisor tells a trainee that her evaluation depends on 'being friendly' after hours. How does the 2026 definition treat this?
options: As quid pro quo harassment: a job decision is linked to accepting sexual conduct
As a performance issue for HR, not harassment
As harassment only if some physical contact occurs, otherwise as a conduct issue for HR
As harassment only if the trainee is a permanent employee
quiz.explanation: The definition covers using acceptance or rejection of sexual conduct, explicitly or implicitly, as a basis for decisions about a person's job.

regulators: Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission (BSEC), for listed banks

references.title: Bank-Company Act, 1991 (Act No. 14 of 1991, as amended up to 2023)
references.issuer: Parliament of Bangladesh (Laws of Bangladesh portal)
references.note: Bangladesh Bank approval of directors and CEOs; fitness bars; at most 20 directors with at least 3 independent (2 if fewer than 20); 3-family-member cap; 12-year limit; alternates; board accountability and audit/risk committees; binding directions; removal of directors; board dissolution for up to two years.

references.title: BRPD Circular No. 02: Formation of Board and Responsibilities of Directors of a Bank-Company
references.note: Board composition and rotation; fit and proper criteria; prior approval within 7 working days; alternates; vacancy and removal; board and chair duties incl. staff training and a code of conduct and ethics; only executive, audit and risk committees; meeting rules; permissive director training.

references.title: BRPD Circular No. 01: Taking Prior Approval of Bangladesh Bank to Appoint Alternate Director in Bank Companies
references.note: An alternate director may not act or attend board or committee meetings without Bangladesh Bank's prior approval; issued under section 15AAA(3).

references.title: BRPD Circular Letter No. 14: Formation of Board and Responsibilities of Directors of a Bank-Company
references.note: Board and committee minutes must record discussions, all observations, notes of dissent in detail and any Bangladesh Bank observer's views; other BRPD Circular 02/2024 instructions are unchanged.

references.title: BRPD-2 Circular No. 03: Guidelines on Internal Control Management System in Banks (July 2026)
references.note: Three lines of defence; HoIA and HoC roles and safeguards; board, audit committee and SMT duties; compliance risk management; mandatory role-based compliance training (5.4.3); observation closure; whistleblower framework; restructure by 31 December 2026.

references.title: BRPD-1 Circular No. 10: Guidelines on Foundation Training for the Newly Recruited Scheduled Bank Officials
references.note: Minimum standard: board-approved policy; at least 14 weeks (8 theory, 6 practice); completion required for confirmation; content includes banking laws, the bank's code of conduct and ethics; five-day rural field stay; certificate.

references.title: Code of Conduct for Banks and Non-Bank Financial Institutions
references.note: Minimum standard for banks: integrity training, use of position, conflicts, outside work, gifts, insider trading, confidentiality, harassment, speak-up, own code circulated within 60 days, ethics committee work plan, signed statement of compliance.

references.title: Bangladesh Labour (Amendment) Act, 2026 (Act No. 43 of 2026)
references.issuer: Parliament of Bangladesh (Laws of Bangladesh portal)
references.provision: Section 4 (new s.2(52A)), section 82 (new s.332) and section 83 (new s.332A)
references.note: Defines sexual harassment incl. quid pro quo; employers must prevent violence and harassment, publicise penalties, adopt a policy, assess risks, inform and train workers, publish complaint procedures; five-member complaints committee led by a woman with two outside members.

references.title: Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006 (Act No. 42 of 2006)
references.issuer: Parliament of Bangladesh (Laws of Bangladesh portal)
references.note: Banks and banking companies are listed as commercial establishments, so the Act's workplace duties reach bank employers.

references.title: Public Interest Information Disclosure (Provide Protection) Act, 2011 (Act No. 7 of 2011)
references.issuer: Parliament of Bangladesh (Laws of Bangladesh portal)
references.note: Good-faith disclosure of public-interest information to an appropriate authority; identity protected without consent; no criminal, civil or departmental case; no demotion, harassing transfer or forced retirement for the discloser.

references.title: Monetary Policy Statement, July-December 2025
references.note: Reports that Bangladesh Bank dissolved and restructured the boards of 15 banks and issued a May 2025 circular tightening transactions with bank-related persons.

references.title: Monetary Policy Statement, January-June 2026
references.note: Reports risk-based supervision from 4 January 2026 with more than 500 Bangladesh Bank officials trained, and new limits on dividends and staff bonuses.

bank.question: Krishnachura's 20-member board has two independent directors. A shareholder says this meets the law because 'two is the minimum'. What is correct?
options: It is fine: two is the minimum for every board size
It falls short: a 20-member board needs at least three independent directors
It is fine if both chair a board committee
It falls short: every board needs at least five independent directors
bank.explanation: Section 15(9) requires at least three independent directors where there are 20 directors; the minimum of two applies only to boards of fewer than 20.

bank.question: Rahman Textiles and Rahman Leather, both controlled by the Rahman family, each want a representative director on a board where two Rahmans already sit as shareholder directors. Under paragraph 3 of BRPD Circular 02/2024, what is the position?
options: Neither may be appointed, since the family already has two seats
Only one may be appointed, because a family may hold only one seat for all the companies it controls
Both may be appointed only if the family drops a shareholder director
Both: beyond family members, up to two representatives of family-controlled companies may sit
bank.explanation: Paragraph 3(e) allows, in addition to family members, no more than two representative directors for companies that the family controls; the separate three-member family limit still applies to the individuals.

bank.question: A company holding Krishnachura shares wants two of its executives on the board as its representatives. What does BRPD Circular 02/2024 allow?
options: Only one representative director per company or institution
Two, if the company holds more than 10% of the shares
Two, provided one is an independent director
As many as its shareholding justifies, up to five
bank.explanation: Paragraph 3(f) says no more than one person may be appointed as representative director on behalf of any company or institution.

bank.question: An individual shareholder who lives abroad asks Krishnachura to appoint his nephew as his 'representative director'. What applies?
options: Allowed if the nephew passes the fitness tests
Allowed for up to three months a year
Not allowed: no one may be a representative director for a natural-person shareholder
Allowed once Bangladesh Bank receives notice of the appointment from the company secretary
bank.explanation: Paragraph 3(g) of BRPD Circular 02/2024 bars appointing anyone as a representative director on behalf of an individual shareholder. The nephew could only join on his own merits and shareholding.

bank.question: A director wants an alternate because he will spend five weeks abroad. What is the position under section 15AAA and BRPD Circular 02/2024?
options: An alternate may serve for five weeks after notifying Bangladesh Bank
An alternate may serve if the board approves by majority
No alternate is possible: the director must be abroad continuously for at least three months
An alternate is possible for any absence from Bangladesh longer than one month in a calendar year
bank.explanation: An alternate may be appointed only for a director who is continuously abroad for at least three months, once a year, for up to three months, and since 2025 only with Bangladesh Bank's prior approval.

bank.question: A director received a notice through Bangladesh Bank under section 17 for an unpaid loan and resigns before the deadline passes. What is the effect?
options: The resignation does not take effect while the notice proceedings are pending
The resignation ends the matter and the loan becomes the bank's problem
The resignation takes effect if the board accepts it
The resignation converts the loan into a director's guarantee
bank.explanation: Paragraph 8(b) of BRPD Circular 02/2024 says a director who has received a section 17 notice cannot transfer his shares until dues are paid, and a resignation during the notice proceedings is not effective.

bank.question: Bangladesh Bank dissolves a bank's board under section 47 for six months and later extends the order. What is the longest the order can last in total?
options: One year including extensions
Three years including extensions
Until the next AGM elects a new board
Two years including extensions
bank.explanation: Section 47(2) allows Bangladesh Bank to extend the order from time to time, but the total period including extensions may not exceed two years.

bank.question: Krishnachura's board wants to remove a director it finds disruptive. What must it do under section 15(4) and paragraph 9 of BRPD Circular 02/2024?
options: Pass a special resolution at an EGM; no approval is needed
Get Bangladesh Bank's prior approval, filing reasons, the board decision and a director list
Remove the director first and then inform Bangladesh Bank in writing within seven days afterwards
Ask the director to resign; removal is never allowed
bank.explanation: Paragraph 9(a) requires prior approval to remove a director of any bank other than a specialised bank, with reasons, the board decision and a director list sent to BRPD-2; removal takes effect from Bangladesh Bank's approval.

bank.question: According to Bangladesh Bank's Monetary Policy Statement for July-December 2025, how many bank boards had it dissolved and restructured?
bank.explanation: The statement reported that Bangladesh Bank had so far dissolved the boards of directors of 15 banks and restructured them to restore effective governance.

bank.question: A candidate was listed as a wilful defaulter by a finance company and was released from the list three years ago. Can he be nominated as a bank director now?
options: Yes: release from the list removes the bar at once
Yes, if he repays any remaining balance first
No: he becomes eligible only five years after release from the list
No: a past wilful defaulter is barred for life
bank.explanation: Paragraph 4(13) of BRPD Circular 02/2024 makes a listed wilful defaulter ineligible until five years have passed after release from the list.

bank.question: A nominee is a director of a general insurance company. Can he become a director of Krishnachura?
options: Yes, because insurers are not banks
No: a director or paid office holder of an insurer is not eligible
Yes, if the insurer is not a subsidiary of the bank
Yes, if he declares the conflict in the minutes
bank.explanation: Paragraph 4(8) excludes anyone serving as director, adviser, consultant or in another paid post at another bank, finance company, insurance company or any of their subsidiaries.

bank.question: Krishnachura's external audit firm's senior partner is nominated as an independent director of Krishnachura. What applies?
options: Eligible once the audit engagement ends at the year end
Eligible as a shareholder director, though not as an independent one, once the audit firm resigns first
Eligible if the audit committee approves it
Not eligible: the bank's own external auditor, lawyer, adviser or consultant cannot be a director
bank.explanation: Paragraph 4(9) bars anyone engaged as the same bank's external auditor, legal adviser, adviser, consultant or in another paid post.

bank.question: Under BRPD Circular 02/2024, for whom does the board itself decide appointments, promotions, transfers and discipline?
options: All officers at head office
All branch managers and heads of divisions at head office
Only the company secretary
The two tiers of officers immediately below the CEO
bank.explanation: Paragraph 10.1(d) leaves HR actions to management under the service rules, except for officers in the two tiers immediately below the CEO, which the board decides.

bank.question: Krishnachura's chair receives a complaint alleging misconduct by the MD/CEO. Under paragraph 10.2 of BRPD Circular 02/2024, how must it be handled?
options: The chair investigates alone and suspends the CEO
Through the board, informing Bangladesh Bank with the CEO's statement
The chair forwards it to the police and waits
The audit committee decides it without informing the board
bank.explanation: Paragraph 10.2(d) says that if a complaint is raised about the CEO, it must be reported to Bangladesh Bank through the board together with the CEO's statement.

bank.question: Can the board chair also chair the executive committee under BRPD Circular 02/2024?
options: No, the executive committee must be chaired by an independent director
No, the board chair may not sit on any committee
Yes, the board chair may also chair the executive committee
Yes, but only for the first year of a term
bank.explanation: Paragraph 11.1(a) allows the board chair to be chair of the executive committee. By contrast, the audit committee chair must be an independent director.

bank.question: An independent director has just finished a three-year term as audit committee chair. Can she be chosen again for the next term?
options: No: an independent director cannot chair the audit committee for two consecutive terms
Yes, if the board votes unanimously
Yes, because only the board chair's two-year term is limited, not the committee chair's term
No: she must also leave the board for three years
bank.explanation: Paragraph 11.2(a) of BRPD Circular 02/2024, repeated in the ICMS guidelines, sets a three-year term and bars an independent director from chairing the audit committee for two consecutive terms.

bank.question: Krishnachura becomes a digital bank. What extra rule applies to its board committees?
options: Committees may meet only online
Each committee must include at least one member with ICT expertise
The risk committee must be chaired by the CTO
An ICT committee becomes the fourth permitted committee
bank.explanation: BRPD Circular 02/2024 and the ICMS guidelines require at least one member with ICT expertise on the committees of a digital bank; the three-committee limit still applies.

bank.question: The board wants to hold a two-day meeting at a resort outside the head office city. What does paragraph 12.1 of BRPD Circular 02/2024 require?
options: Nothing, if the bank pays the costs from its training budget
Informing Bangladesh Bank within seven days after the meeting, with the minutes and the total cost
Approval from the shareholders at the next AGM
Applying for Bangladesh Bank's prior approval seven working days ahead, with reasons and costs
bank.explanation: Board and committee meetings must be held in the head office city; an exceptional meeting elsewhere needs a prior approval application seven working days in advance, and needless costs must be avoided.

bank.question: At least how many meetings a year must the audit committee and the risk management committee each hold?
options: Four
Two
Six
Twelve
bank.explanation: Both BRPD Circular 02/2024 (for the risk committee) and the ICMS guidelines (section 2.4.2.4, for the audit committee) require at least four meetings a year, with more as needed.

bank.question: Who certifies to the board each year on the effectiveness of the bank's internal control policy, practice and procedure under the ICMS guidelines?
options: The Head of Internal Audit
The external auditor
The senior management team led by the MD/CEO
The chair of the risk management committee
bank.explanation: Section 2.4.3.5 requires the SMT to review the control system's effectiveness yearly and give the board a yearly certification.

bank.question: The Head of Internal Audit wants to join Krishnachura's senior management team as a full member. What do the guidelines say?
options: The HoIA must be a full SMT member to understand the business
The HoIA may join if the audit committee agrees
The HoIA may not be an SMT member but must attend SMT meetings as an observer
The HoIA may neither join nor attend SMT meetings
bank.explanation: Section 2.4.3.2 says the HoIA shall not be a member of the SMT but must attend its meetings as an observer.

bank.question: Under section 2.3.3.8, how much planned mandatory leave must ICMS officials take each year, and why?
options: Ten days, planned confidentially, to help prevent and detect fraud and money laundering
Five days, to allow training
Fifteen days, as a wellbeing benefit
Twenty days a year, split into several blocks at each employee's own choice and convenience
bank.explanation: Unit heads prepare a confidential mandatory annual leave plan of 10 days per year for ICMS staff, in the spirit of AML and fraud prevention; the management may change it but the employee cannot claim a change.

bank.question: An auditor moved from the Credit Division to internal audit six months ago. The audit plan assigns her to review the Credit Division's work from her time there. What applies?
options: She may audit it because she knows the process best
She may audit it with her new manager's approval
She may audit it after one year in internal audit
She must not audit work she performed in her previous department
bank.explanation: Section 2.3.3.6 says internal audit officials shall not audit their own work from their previous departments or offices.

bank.question: Which of these does the Compliance Function's 'Policies and Governance' division handle under section 2.2.2.1?
options: Conducting surprise branch audits
Supporting the code of conduct, compliance culture and ethics
Approving loans above the CEO's delegated limit on behalf of the board
Running the bank's treasury dealing desk
bank.explanation: Section 2.2.2.1(c) gives this division compliance policies and SOPs, alignment with regulation and support for governance frameworks such as the code of conduct, compliance culture and ethics.

bank.question: A compliance breach could lead to a large Bangladesh Bank fine. Under section 5.3.3.6, when must it reach the board or audit committee?
options: Immediately
At the next quarterly compliance report
At the year-end internal control review
Only after the fine is imposed
bank.explanation: Significant compliance breaches must be reported immediately to the board or audit committee where there is a significant risk of legal or regulatory sanctions, financial loss or reputational damage.

bank.question: Section 5.4.1 requires a formal regulatory change management process. Which of these is part of it?
options: Waiting for Bangladesh Bank to explain each new circular in a meeting
Sending new circulars only to the branches that ask for them
Assessing a new rule's impact and updating policies, procedures and systems
Asking internal audit to rewrite policies after each circular
bank.explanation: Banks must identify and track new and amended rules, assess their impact, disseminate them to the business, and ensure policies, procedures and systems are updated.

bank.question: Krishnachura's compliance team runs one generic annual quiz for all staff and calls it the 'role-based programme'. In an inspection, what is the most likely gap against section 5.4.3?
options: The training was not delivered by trainers certified by Bangladesh Bank's training academy
The curriculum is not built on the compliance risk assessment or tailored to roles
The quiz was not translated into English
The training was not approved by shareholders
bank.explanation: Section 5.4.3 requires a mandatory programme that is role-based, with a curriculum based on the CRA and measured effectiveness. A single generic quiz for all staff misses the first two.

bank.question: Which statement best describes the relationship of the three ICMS functions in section 1.7.4?
options: Audit sets the rules, compliance measures risk and risk management approves products
All three functions report to the MD/CEO and share one head
Compliance replaces internal audit in banks using the three lines model
Risk identifies risks, compliance sets and checks rules, audit assures both
bank.explanation: Section 1.7.4 describes risk management, compliance and audit as linked pillars: risk sets what to manage, compliance the rules, and audit validates how well both work.

bank.question: A branch officer asks a member of parliament to call the MD about her transfer request. Which part of the Code does this breach?
options: The rules on accepting foreign awards
The rule on keeping information confidential after an employee leaves the bank
The rules on dress and grooming
The ban on using political or board influence for transfers
bank.explanation: Section 11 of the Code forbids any employee, directly or indirectly, from approaching a member of parliament or using political or board influence for employment, promotion, transfer or other personal gain.

bank.question: Under section 37 of the Code, what must a bank's ethics committee do?
options: Approve every gift staff receive
Have an annual work plan and periodically monitor progress against it
Investigate every whistleblower report itself
Sign each employee's statement of compliance
bank.explanation: Section 37(ii) says the ethics committee shall have an annual work plan and monitor progress against it, promote the code and lead by example.

bank.question: A former Krishnachura officer joins a competitor and shares a list of large depositors with his new employer. Which Code duty has he broken?
options: The duty to circulate the code within 60 days
The duty to seek permission for outside employment
The duty to keep confidential information secret after leaving the bank
No duty, since the Code ends when employment ends
bank.explanation: Sections 27 and 36 require information obtained in employment to stay confidential and secure even after the employee leaves.

bank.question: Which channels does section 8.4.2 of the ICMS guidelines expect a bank to offer whistleblowers?
options: Email or hotline, a secure online system, and sealed confidential letters
A suggestion box at each branch, emptied by the branch manager
Reports through the line manager only, so that the normal chain of command is respected
A public social media page where staff can post concerns
bank.explanation: Section 8.4.2 lists multiple confidential channels: email or hotline, a secure online reporting system, and sealed letters marked confidential to the HoC, the audit committee chair or Bangladesh Bank.

bank.question: After the preliminary assessment of a whistleblower report, to whom are the investigation's findings and recommendations submitted under section 8.4.5?
options: The MD/CEO
The chair of the audit committee
The head of HR
The person named in the report
bank.explanation: Section 8.4.5 says the findings and recommendations are documented for submission to the chair of the audit committee.

bank.question: Krishnachura's HR head proposes to lower a whistleblower's annual rating because 'her report caused disruption'. What is the position?
options: Permitted if the report was not proved
Permitted if the lower rating also reflects other genuine work issues recorded during the year
Permitted after one year has passed
Prohibited: retaliation is barred, and Bangladesh Bank may act against a bank that retaliates
bank.explanation: Section 8.4.4 bars demotion, suspension, harassment or any retaliation, protects good-faith reports even if unproved, and says Bangladesh Bank may act against retaliating banks.

bank.question: Under the Public Interest Information Disclosure Act 2011, may a person's identity be revealed after a protected disclosure?
options: Not without that person's consent
Yes, once the investigation starts
Yes, if the accused asks the court
Yes, to the person's employer only
bank.explanation: Section 5(1) of the Act says the identity of a person who makes a public-interest disclosure shall not be revealed without his or her consent.

bank.question: An officer spots possible fraud by her own branch manager. Which route best fits the Code and the ICMS framework?
options: Report it to the branch manager first, because the Code says fraud goes to your immediate superior
Investigate quietly and collect evidence herself before reporting
Use a confidential whistleblower channel, since the normal route runs through him
Post it anonymously on social media to warn customers
bank.explanation: Section 16 of the Code expects fraud to be reported, and the ICMS framework offers confidential channels to the HoC or audit committee chair, which suit cases involving the superior. Social media posting breaches the confidentiality and media rules.

bank.question: Under the new section 332(1), what must an employer publish on its website?
options: The names of all complainants and accused persons
The full minutes of every complaints committee meeting, within thirty days
Related reports and a description of its complaint-handling procedure
The salaries of complaints committee members
bank.explanation: Section 332(1)(h) requires the workplace website to provide related reports and a description of the complaint management procedure; confidentiality of individuals still applies.

bank.question: Krishnachura's complaints committee has five members: a woman chair from HR, three male officers and one member from a women's rights organisation. What is wrong under section 332A?
options: Women are not in the majority, and only one outside member has been appointed
Nothing: five members led by a woman is enough
The chair must come from an outside organisation
A committee may not include any men
bank.explanation: Section 332A needs five members, a majority of women from within the establishment, a woman as head and two members from organisations working on gender and sexual violence. This committee has three men out of five and only one external member.

bank.question: Which of these does the 2026 definition of sexual harassment expressly list?
options: Assigning a fair workload based on job grade
Giving negative but accurate performance feedback
Refusing a leave request because of staffing needs
Taking still or video images for blackmail or to damage someone's reputation
bank.explanation: The new section 2(52A) lists conduct such as unwelcome physical contact, sexual remarks, showing pornography, sexually suggestive messages and taking images for blackmail or character assassination.

bank.question: Under the new section 332(1), the employer must consider violence and harassment in which management system?
options: Credit risk management, including the early-warning system for large loans
Occupational safety and health management, including psychosocial risks
IT change management
Asset-liability management
bank.explanation: Section 332(1)(e) requires employers to take necessary steps in occupational safety and health management, considering violence, harassment and related psychosocial risks.

bank.question: Who must approve a scheduled bank's own foundation training policy and modules under BRPD-1 Circular 10?
options: The bank's board of directors (or local highest authority for a foreign bank)
Bangladesh Bank's training academy
The Bangladesh Institute of Bank Management
The Head of Compliance alone, after consulting the bank's own training institute
bank.explanation: Paragraph 2 of the guidelines requires banks to prepare their own policies and modules aligned with the guidelines, approved by the board or, for foreign banks, the local highest authority.

bank.question: Which practical element does BRPD-1 Circular 10 require in foundation training?
options: A month posted at Bangladesh Bank's head office
A week of foreign exchange dealing on a live desk
A field stay of at least five days to study the rural economy, followed by a report
An overseas study visit to a regional bank
bank.explanation: Paragraph 7(a)(c) requires practical exposure to the rural economy through a minimum five-day field stay, focusing on SME and agricultural projects, with a report and presentation.

bank.question: Which set of documents best shows Bangladesh Bank that Krishnachura's compliance training meets section 5.4.3 of the ICMS guidelines?
options: A signed attendance sheet from the annual town-hall meeting on compliance chaired by the MD
The CRA, a role-to-module map, test results and the quarterly committee report
The trainers' CVs and the training centre's floor plan
Copies of the circulars emailed to all staff
bank.explanation: Section 5.4.3 requires a mandatory role-based programme built on the CRA, with effectiveness measured and reported. The evidence must show each element, not just attendance.
